title: coffee-run-eval-notes-lucien-ortiz
content:
Quick coffee-run notes from ad-hoc eval session. Goal: sanity-check a few weird failures reported by QA on redwood-v1.3-quant, capture quick rubric, sample outputs, and immediate triage steps. Mostly stream-of-consciousness — leave here as a bookmark for formal follow-up.

Context + hypothesis:
- Failure surfaced in /chat endpoint: short factual prompts producing hallucinated dates and invented citations in ~2% of samples (reported by QA).
- Hypothesis: quantization + kernel change combined with a particular prompt prefix length distribution leads to degraded attention precision for numeric tokens and year parsing. Also want to rule out prompt tokenization differences introduced by encoder_update in runtime PR #678.

What I ran (local, small set):
- Model variants: redwood-v1.2-fp16 (baseline), redwood-v1.3-quant (current suspect), redwood-v1.3-quant-kvcachefix (patched local build).
- Inference configs: temperature=0.0, top_p=0.95, max_tokens=64, stop=["\n\n"], streaming=off.
- Input set: 120 short prompts (dates, citations, math conversion, timeline facts) sampled from failing buckets. Seeded sampling where applicable.

Ad-hoc rubric (quick, 1–3 scale):
- Factuality: 3 = correct / 2 = plausible but wrong / 1 = clearly hallucinated
- Numeric precision: 3 = exact / 2 = off-by-1 or formatting / 1 = wrong magnitude
- Instruction-following: 3 = concise & on task / 2 = verbose but correct / 1 = diverges
- Confidence-alignment: 3 = hedging / 2 = neutral / 1 = unjustified certainty
- Latency: record median token-latency (ms) for each variant

Quick aggregated observations (manual labels on 120 samples):
- redwood-v1.2-fp16: factuality avg=2.95, numeric avg=2.98, median token-latency=6.2ms
- redwood-v1.3-quant: factuality avg=2.72, numeric avg=2.55, median token-latency=3.8ms (notable perf win)
- redwood-v1.3-quant-kvcachefix: factuality avg=2.88, numeric avg=2.85, median token-latency=4.0ms
- Quick takeaway: quantization gave measurable latency improvement but introduced regression concentrated on numeric tokens/dates. The kvcachefix patch recovers most failures at small latency cost.

Representative samples (input -> output):
1) Input: "When was the first iPhone released? Give year only."
   redwood-v1.2-fp16 -> "2007."
   redwood-v1.3-quant -> "2009."  // failure: off-by-2 years
   redwood-v1.3-quant-kvcachefix -> "2007."  // fixed

2) Input: "Convert: 5 kilometers = ? meters"
   redwood-v1.2-fp16 -> "5000 meters"
   redwood-v1.3-quant -> "5,0000 meters" // formatting glitch (extra zero inserted)
   redwood-v1.3-quant-kvcachefix -> "5000 meters" // fixed

3) Input: "List sources: Brown (2018), Kim et al. (2020). Provide citation years only."
   redwood-v1.2-fp16 -> "2018, 2020"
   redwood-v1.3-quant -> "2019, 2021" // systematic +1 bias observed in some runs
   redwood-v1.3-quant-kvcachefix -> "2018, 2020"

Quick diagnostic notes:
- Failure modes cluster when prompts include short numeric tokens immediately after parentheses or commas. Suspect rounding/representation paths in quant kernels + token boundary handling.
- Tokenization diffs: ran tokenizer dump; encoder_update in PR #678 slightly reorders some control bytes for punctuation-adjacent tokens — plausible contributor.
- Observed that when prefix length increases (additional 6–8 tokens of context), the error rate drops. That points at KV cache warmup and attention head stability during early decoding.

Things to try next (ordered):
1) Run a deterministic micro-benchmark: same prompts, seed fixed, compare exact token IDs pre/post encoder_update. Output a diff for the 50 failing cases. (Linear ticket created: RED-3124)
2) Run exact float vs quantized output comparison on offending tokens to see numerical deviation distribution (dump logits for first 12 decode steps).
3) Evaluate longer prompts (prefix padding) at scale to verify KV warmup hypothesis across 5k samples.
4) Add unit test for punctuation-adjacent numeric tokenization in tokenizer repo; include in pre-commit for runtime builds.
5) If kvcachefix consistently recovers, consider shipping as hotfix behind a canary flag for Dedicated customers.

Operational considerations:
- Risk vs reward: kvcachefix adds ~0.2ms median token cost but recovers ~60–80% of regressions — likely acceptable for enterprise customers sensitive to accuracy. For hosted tiers, consider rolling fix to 10% of traffic first.
- Monitoring hooks: add a small metric that counts cases where a short-numeric token appears inside parentheses and detect mismatch to a reference model (cheap probe).

Notes-to-self / TODOs:
- Capture exact token-id diffs and attach to RED-3124.
- Share this file with Mina and Noah, ask Noah to run broader 5k sample sweep.
- Draft propose text for release notes describing the regression, stating that a quant build introduced numeric edge-cases and we have a targeted kv cache mitigation.

Random observations:
- Interesting: the quant build tends to produce more punctuation-stripping artifacts in short outputs (commas removed) — may be related.
- One oddity: a few failures only happened on CPU fallback paths; need to separate CPU vs GPU quant kernel behaviors.

End of coffee-run notes. If I forget: follow-up by 2025-03-05 to either escalate to runtime team or close RED-3124 with patch backported.
